stories.headline: Kilnmouth partners up with the works!
body: The council has spoken: Kilnmouth holds with Glimmerwell. Warm rooms, steady work. Have a bright day!

stories.headline: Kilnmouth stays split after the vote
body: Seven chairs and still two sides. Kilnmouth's hold is split; the kiln yard calls it "honest".

stories.headline: Hall 5: a fifth Seal at the Kilnmouth kiln
body: Master Tobias Hearn's Trial Hall is lit again, and a holder has earned the Kilnmouth Seal.
The kiln was lit with company coal. The Master says it burns the same. He did not sound pleased about that.

stories.headline: Brightgate to Keeper guests: free, polite, shut
body: Glimmerwell's home city lets a Keeper Cadet walk anywhere. Everything is free and polite.
Every real door is "by appointment". The lobby's visitors' hours end at five. It is always five.

stories.headline: Hall 4: a Keeper Cadet wins the Brightgate Seal
body: In Old Wick, under a dead lightning rod, Master Ada Coil gave a Keeper Cadet the Brightgate Seal.
Her Hall was built for storms. She says the sky over Brightgate stays calm now, and she misses the noise.

replies.name: Old Wick neighbour
replies.text: Ada cheers for real lightning. We have not had any in years. She cheered anyway.

stories.headline: The first Calm Tower stands idle
body: Behind a fence in the Lamp Works stands a grey tower with dark lamps. Above it, the sky still moves.
Kilnmouth's tower was fitted at the Lamp Works too. Nobody here will say why that one was switched on.

stories.headline: Old Wick still burns three flame lanterns
body: In Brightgate's old quarter three flame lanterns still burn, trimmed by a lamplighter every dusk.
The Post salutes any town that keeps an old light. Even this one.

stories.headline: Neighbour Rook races a Cadet to the Hall door
body: Rook, company staff now, raced a Keeper Cadet to the Old Wick Hall door and battled them on the steps.
Asked who won, Rook said there was an empty desk next to his. That was not an answer.

stories.headline: Courtesy Cruisers: here to reassure you!
body: Our Courtesy Cruisers glide on the hum: no wheels, no rotors, nothing to worry about. Sky Concierges up top!
Wave at a Cruiser today. It will not wave back, but it appreciates you. Have a bright day!

stories.headline: Glow Care: members only, smiles for all
body: Glow Care is our member clinic for Walklings. The door is shut for privacy. Comfort is our first word!

stories.headline: Parade day: the President speaks on Charter Hill
body: Rotor craft, marching Officers, tanks and the President's car came through Lantern Square to Charter Hill.
In his first speech in person, the President said a Keeper will stand on every road and at every Hall.

replies.name: Square regular
replies.text: Saw half his face between two flags. The flags looked very official.

stories.headline: Picking Day closed to civilians
body: From the speech: Picking Day, the draw that gives a civilian their first Walkling, is closed to them.
Holders who already walk with Walklings are not affected. Families with a name in the draw are.

stories.headline: Speech: schools to be re-taught
body: Also said: the schools re-taught; anyone standing with Glimmerwell in public fined or jailed.
No line of the speech mentioned the company's own permits. The Post checked twice.

stories.headline: Every Roof a Lantern, and the Rotor overhead
body: The band played "Every Roof a Lantern" as the Lantern Rotor crossed. No lyrics. Everyone hummed.

stories.headline: The Muster Hall: chained since the Great War
body: Beside the Dojo stands the Muster Hall, chained shut since the Great War. It is High Charity's Trial Hall.
The chain comes off, the door Keeper says, for a holder with seven Seals on the roll. Not before.

replies.name: Lantern Square porter
replies.text: I polish that chain on Fridays. Seems a shame nobody ever gets to take it off.

stories.headline: What the Great War left in the capital
body: The Great War is long over. Some of what it left is still here: an old roll of Seals, and a chained hall.
The Post remembers it gently, as the old ones tell it: the lanterns stayed lit through all of it.

stories.headline: Fernbrook Trial Hall reopens under the Keepers
body: Master Fen has signed the Keepers' order and her Hall is open again. The cordon is gone from the door.
Fen offers one rematch to holders who earned her Seal before. The Post recommends a snack first.

stories.headline: Fernbrook Hall reopens as a demo hall!
body: Master Fen's Hall is open again as a Glimmerwell demo hall. Partnership looks lovely on an orchard Master!
Come for a rematch, stay for the lanterns. Have a bright day!

voices.text: Every new holder runs to the Lodge. Nobody walks to the Lodge. I have checked.
'A bond grows in small jobs.' Today's small job was finding my Walkling. Bond: strong.
My Walkling went GLOWING after a good day of care. I went GLOWING after a good lunch.
Turned up with zero Acorns once. Same bed, same blanket, same Della.
The Schoolhouse says Lanternball Court is a distraction. The Schoolhouse is wrong.
Said my piece. Stepped back. Felt extremely lawful for the rest of the day.
Up late. The watch walked by. I waved. The watch waved back, lawfully.
Rook took the starter that beats yours. He will tell you. He told me, and I was not even there.
Tall grass hides shy Walklings. It also hid my left shoe. Both are fine now.
Climbed a hill for better signal. Then remembered who owns the poles from this hill to the coast.
Rain day. Different Walklings out in the grass. My socks have made their peace with it.
Took a free lantern. Felt brighter by nature for about an hour. Then just felt like me.
A Pomlet sat in the basket I needed. Now I need a different basket.
Master Fen is out in the orchard again. The Hall is very tidy and very empty.
Somebody opened the crates at the gate. Associate Tobin reread the memo. Twice.
Quarterly targets are a team sport! Bring your own crate. Kidding! We bring the crates.
The old tunnels have the best echo on the ridge. Do not test this at night.
Saw the floating computer. It did not see me. I think. The screen was dark.
That census tent has more clipboards than I have socks. And I pack a lot of socks.
"Path reopened by Glimmerwell Co. crews!" The exclamation mark is theirs. The mud is mine.
Rain on Route 2 is the best rain. Ask any Walkling who just found a puddle.
Hush isn't a rule in Wickerglen. It's a personality.
"I just hold the lamp," he says. Sure. And I just stand near the snacks.
"Quarterly review, sweetie." She says it so sweetly. I have never been more nervous.
The lamps are off and the glen looks like itself again. I'd forgotten its real colour.
Tiptoed through the glen at night. Something snored. Hoping it was a Walkling.
Rule one in Cobblecrest: look down. Rule two: that's a Pebblit. Rule three: say sorry.
Hale says forty years he dug beside Walklings. Looks like he's got forty more in him.
Fair and square, the Reeve says. Square, sure. Fair, I'm still chewing on.
The desk at Bright Quarry is very clean. Clerk Mint is very polite. The stone is still stone.
Cobblecrest miners built the Old Weir. Gran says it is the only thing in town that never complains.
Hale opened the seam again. The whole quarry sounds like a lazy afternoon.
Stamped BRINEWICK so many times today I'm signing my letters with it.
Asked what year it is. Got a smile and a shrug. Mahopac's like that.
Looked through the lens expecting stars. Got my own childhood instead. Rude, but fair.
"Eat up. The world can wait." Best advice in the woods, and it came from a dream.
Every roof, every night. Visitors ask if the lanterns get tired. Do you?
The marina Walklings know which bench is mine. They sit on it first. On purpose.
Six of us. Five games. One rule: nobody touches my high score.
First lesson: be kind in the streets. Then fractions. Kindness was easier.
No Seal on the line here, so nobody cries. Well. Less crying.
A Walkling tried to deposit a leaf. The queue voted to let it. The queue was overruled.
Ribbit rides our wires. Post nicely. We read it all, but we like the nice ones best.
Citizen. Say your piece, then step back. Then maybe one more step. Thank you.
Wine vest, mandatory smile, quarterly target. Have a bright day! I mean it. I have to.
My partner stares at the ceiling sometimes, like it heard a phone ring. Nothing rang.
The hum is normal. I hummed back once. Nothing happened. Should something have happened?
The Shipping Ledger Office has more pages than this road has steps. I'd know. I walk both.
Saw a Quiet one. Took one step closer. It went Humming. I took two steps back.
Rain on the Brinewick road, and the hum doesn't stop for it. Neither do we. Walkling under my coat.
The tide's out. Sit a while. Captain's orders, more or less.
Came in for rope. Left with rope and a Walkling asleep in my bag. Good trade.
Our Lantern Host still has no name tag. Heals you anyway. Explains it slower than the tide.
Since the crate business, I knock on every depot crate I pass. Just in case.
Night on the west pier. Water slapping, lanterns low, one Walkling snoring on a rope coil.
The clouds over that grey tower look ironed. I don't trust ironed clouds.
Every plan in Hearthmoor starts with 'meet me by the Plaza sign.' Every plan ends with someone late.
The West watch nodded at my Walkling before it nodded at me. I know my place now.
Lantern night on the Plaza. My Walkling fell asleep halfway through. Best review it could give.
Asked when The Parked Coach is leaving. Got a very long look. Seemed like a fair question to me.
Went into Stitch & Lantern for one thing. My Walkling chose a second thing. We left with both.
Clear day on Lanternball Court. Three Walklings on the sideline, all convinced they're the ball.
Heard it through the window again: 'A bond grows in small jobs.' Then the sound of a broom. Classic.
Got offered a chair at Keeper House. Sat very straight in it. Nobody said I was allowed to slouch.
Clerk Wynn found my form before I'd finished asking for it. I was not ready for that much service.
Tilly says Buddy helps with spelling. Lizzy says Buddy sits. Honestly, both can be true.
The drip in 5B keeps better time than I do. Somebody please mention it to Mr. Gristle. Again.
Sat still by the tall grass long enough for a shy Walkling to sit still too. We called it a draw.
Route 1 at night: every rustle is a shy Walkling, the breeze or my nerves. Two out of three, nice.
Snow on Route 1. Followed tiny tracks for ages. Turned out they were mine, from earlier.
Asked a Pomlet to get off my ladder. It looked at me like I was the visitor. Fair, honestly.
Juniper says 'Brighter by nature!' every single time. Now I say it back. I can't stop. Send help.
The grey Fuzzwick watches the lanterns like it's waiting for one of them to say something.
Practised BLOOM matchups all night. Forgot I'd have to say hello to Master Fen first. Nerves.
Rook said the Pomlets looked grey going in. Said it quietly. Then didn't say much of anything.
Asked Ken the way to the lab. Kit disagreed. Clerk Jed pointed. The ridge runs on second opinions.
Dr. Weller said good morning to my Walkling first. Decent people, they told me. They weren't wrong.
Walked the old tunnels now the crates are open. Just echoes. I said hello. Hello said hello.
I don't count glow, I count clipboards. We're one short. Again.
Glimmerwell crews reopened the path. Lovely. Could they reopen my knees next?
Dusk again already? Days out here walk faster than I do.
My Walkling made a trail in the snow. I followed it. Now we're both lost, but together.
Sat on a root. The root was asleep. The root was a Walkling. Apologised to both.
Haven't heard "Quarterly review, sweetie" since the lamps went off. I miss nothing.
That quiet associate looks at his lamp like it owes him an answer.
Rain in the glen sounds like someone whispering "hush" on repeat. Best rain there is.
Glow sharing is a partnership. My partner is asleep. Still sharing, I'm told.
Garnet explains healing like it's the first time, every time. It is not my first time.
Shopkeeper Dottie says she knows every Pebblit in town. I don't believe her. A bit I do.
The Reeve still says fair and square. She just says it slower every week.
The Acquisitions man said "units". My Pebblit sat on his shoe. Fair trade.
Watched at the Stone Hall. Master Hale looked at me once. I've been training ever since.
Saw a lad step off a cart and not look back. Good for him. Good for us.
The Keeper scout nodded at me, then wrote something down. I hope it said "nice hat".
Clerk Mint says everything here is a partnership. The crates haven't signed anything.
Walked home in the dark and stepped on nothing. The Pebblits moved for me, for once.
Mom said small jobs. Nobody said the small job was a whole time-snagged woods.
Said hello to Bess. She said hello like we'd already met. Maybe we had. Mahopac.
The lens showed my seventh birthday at a bowling alley. I still can't bowl.
Night at the observatory: clear sky, quiet woods, and a lens that keeps its own notes.
I come for the airships. My Walkling comes for the crumbs. We both leave happy.
Best neighbours in the capital, the Barracks. Quiet, polite, and they notice everything. Everything.
Three laps of the Mall before lunch. My Walkling did one, then sat on my foot for the rest.
Nobody steals a parcel at the Keeper Apartments. Nobody would dare. Lovely place. Very watched.
It says Charity right there in the name. I still wouldn't stand between a holder and a win.
Warden Ilse's invite got me into the Event Hall. Nothing gets me out of losing at it.
My own rule at the Dojo: lose here, so you lose less at a Trial Hall. Working so far. Mostly.
We were told to be quiet while the Lantern Council sat. We were. Mostly. Somebody sneezed.
Operator Rue could read out a shopping list on that radio and I'd still sit up straight.
Asked Archivist Mo what the five Answerers answer. Mo showed me the page. Very neat. Very blank.
Sergeant Drummond minds the Keeper House door like it might wander off. Kindly, but firmly.
Care and kindness, they said. I did both. Now Lantern Houses save me a bed. Kindness pays in naps.
Rook waited at the Route 3 gate like a good Neighbour. Arms crossed. Pretending he wasn't waiting.
Walked by the Comfort Sanctuary. Very comfortable name. Very quiet room. I walked a little faster.
A Cordhound followed me a little way, then stopped. I checked for a lead. No lead.
A Humwisp at night is just the hum with a face. I said goodnight. It said hum.
Marisol runs the ferry and the Tide Hall. I asked her how. She said sit a while. I'm still sitting.
The Glimmerwell Depot is very tidy. Tidy enough to make you wonder about the tidy crates.
Dorian Pell said 'units' on the quay. My Walkling went and sat right in his shadow. On purpose.
Rain on the west pier. The ferry doesn't mind. Being wet is most of a ferry's job.
Marisol handed over the Brinewick Seal like she was lending a rope. Then straight back to the ferry.
The Capital Partner said 'Policy is kindness, written down.' So I wrote it down. Felt very policy.
Three lanyards now. They clink when I walk. My unit tilts its head at the clink. Probably nothing.
Learning the words: unit, partnership, quarterly target. Glow sharing I'm in no rush to learn.
I stamp the lids. I don't open them. That's the job, and the job pays.
The tally sheet has a column for colour. I never asked why. I stopped wanting to.
Since the fitting, mine stops on the path and listens. To what, I couldn't tell you.
Same company, new paint. I knew it back when it still made medicine.
The hum is normal. I say it every hour. It helps me more than it helps them.
The lamp pulses like a heartbeat. My Walkling's skips when it gets close.
The review has a line for every unit I logged. It has no line for how they looked.
He asked about the facility. Now his desk is empty. 'Transferred north,' they said.
Slept under a wire set that would not stop talking. Fen was awake the whole night.
They say a Seal went dull in the Commander's hand, then came back. Seals know whose they are.
"A Seal is not for sale." Nobody asked to buy one. Now everybody is wondering who did.
My gran says the Seal roll goes back to the Great War. She says it the way you say "old roof".
Wiped forty lenses. Every one hummed like it was pleased with me. I was not pleased with it.
Nobody led them. They walked to the hum like it was calling them home for supper.
Man by the weir waves at me every morning. Never says hello. Writes something down after.
Keepers on the lanes again. Fen's trees look like they slept for the first time in a week.
A lantern on my gate I did not ask for. It is a nice lantern. That is what bothers me.
Keepers buy apples on the left of the stall. Glimmerwell buys on the right. I sell to the middle.
New hire keeps a hand on one pocket. Everyone here has a pocket like that. I do not ask about mine.
A Host carried a letter out by hand today. Off the wire. Up here that is the loudest thing going.
Somebody walked the whole west watch and admired the chalk. The chalk artist is still beaming.
East sign stands. Count closed. Thank you, citizen. Step back. Have some tea.
Lantern night. Pryce lit them slow, so we could watch every one catch.
One of the old ones hums along with the kettle now. In tune, mostly.
Host Amos keeps one window dark on purpose. He says the dark helps the cots sleep.
Saw them on Ribbit in a company lanyard. Now a pin. Busy autumn, holder.
Somebody on our lane put a lanyard in a drawer and a pin on their coat. The drawer squeaks.
Light on in that kitchen till late. Maze sat in the window like a lamp of her own.
Mrs. Calloway says a kid on our lane does "important work" now. She said it twice.
Juniper packed up her stand before supper. Left one lantern on the bench. It is still on.
Juniper says a holder went all mysterious on her. "Very Keeper of them," she says, fondly.
West for the capital, east for the hills. Most people stand here a minute, reading the post.
Adders on the walls means weather. I have never been wrong. I have often been rained on.
I have watched one reed for an hour. It blinked. I am staying until it does it again.
Nobody comes down to the beds. Sit, or battle. Most people battle. Willow likes good hands.
Bin tipped over in the night. Rubbish sorted into little piles by morning. Nobody owns up.
"In order. I checked it myself." He means it. That is what makes it worth listening to.
A Cadet sat in the Governor's good chair today. Nobody gets the good chair. I polished it after.
Cadet came back from Charter Hill and went straight to the Warden. Not on the wire. In person.
Two came up the trail together. One went home early to put the kettle on.
Kids in coats at the bathhouse. In Kilnmouth! My nan would not believe it.
Reeve Agna counts hands like a baker counts loaves. Three and three. Again. Again.
Gauge is another notch down. I stopped checking. My knees check for me.
Dray grew up in that bathhouse. Runs the tower crew now. Says "the works", never the company name.
The retired Keeper stands by the post like he never retired. Very polite. Very by the book.
No storm again! The tower is the best thing that ever happened here.
Curfew night, the works kept a warm room open for a family. Say what you like. It was warm.
Ask Orla a question and she hands you a bucket. You end up with the answer and a clean floor.
Wine vests carrying coal up the Hall steps. Nobody asked. Everybody watched.
Works plate on the council door now. Warm room all winter, they say. I will believe the warm.
Keepers hold the town. Good. Now somebody tell the cloud.
"Visitors' hours end at five. It's five." She said it at ten in the morning.
Everything is free here. Every door I tried was by appointment. The bench was free. I sat.
Master Ada says storms are not stopped, only moved. She says it to the sky, mostly.
Three flame lanterns, one lamplighter, every dusk. The company lamps hum. These just burn.
A Courtesy Cruiser parked outside my house to "reassure" me. I was fine before it came.
My boy's name was in for Picking Day. Now it isn't.
Tanks in the square, no guns on them. Big and quiet. Like a cat that wants you to know it's there.
A guard led a woman in a wine vest past me. She looked at the Cadet pins, not the faces.
Shut since the war, holder. Come back with seven on the roll. That is the whole speech, every day.
No words to the anthem, so everybody hums their own. Sounds better than any words would.
Fen picked her side in front of everyone. Then she went and watered the trees like it was any day.
All our Walklings looked at the hill at once. Miss Lizzy said "eyes front". Even she looked.
Lizzy wants to know which lesson the holder is now: lanyard or pin. She says teachers have to know.
Jars on the weir hut sill now. The man inside writes something down every time one is added.
Archivist Mo has five full pages and one blank one. He reads the blank one most.
The Junior Bright from Hearthmoor keeps telling a Cadet there is an empty desk next to his.

notices.title: LANTERN HOUSE: REST UP
notices.text: Hurt or tired? Della has beds. 5 Acorns, or what you have, or free at 0.

notices.title: FROM KEEPER HOUSE
notices.text: Walk beside wild Walklings, not ahead of them. Feed, rest, listen. Thank you, citizen.

notices.title: FOUND: ONE SCARF
notices.text: Left by Lanternball Court. Smells strongly of Walkling. Ask at Keeper House.

notices.title: SEEN: ONE SLEEPY WALKLING
notices.text: Napping on Market Row since breakfast. Not lost. Just very comfortable. Let it be.

notices.title: KEEPER1: CARRY IT
notices.text: Every holder must carry a free Keeper1. Officer Ness issues them on Route 1.

notices.title: LOST: ONE BALL
notices.text: Last seen rolling into the tall grass. A shy Walkling may be keeping it. Let it.

notices.title: ON FADE
notices.text: Lantern Houses do not cure Fade. Care does. Host Amos will explain, kindly.

notices.title: FERNBROOK TRIAL HALL
notices.text: Master Fen tests holders for a Seal. If the Hall is empty, try the orchard.

notices.title: KEEPER STANDING
notices.text: Care and kindness earn Standing. Trusted holders find a Lantern House bed saved.

notices.title: FREE GLIMMER LANTERNS
notices.text: Brighter by nature! Free lanterns at the Fernbrook stand. It's a partnership!

notices.title: FEELING TIRED?
notices.text: Tired is just relaxed with bad lighting! Ask a wine vest. Have a bright day!

notices.title: CLIMB THE TIERS
notices.text: Guest, Associate, Junior Bright, Bright Lead. Your next tier is one quota away!

notices.title: HEIGHTS: TUNNELS QUIET
notices.text: The night crates are open and the old tunnels are quiet. Leave a light. Leave them wild.

notices.title: ROUTE 2: WALK BESIDE
notices.text: Walk beside wild Walklings, not ahead of them. Feed, rest, listen. The Keepers.

notices.title: FOUND: ONE MITTEN
notices.text: Left on a flat stone by the Route 2 path. Damp but cheerful. Its twin is out there.

notices.title: COUNT WITH THE CENSUS
notices.text: Every Census log counts toward Standing. Tired is just relaxed with bad lighting!

notices.title: HUSH, PLEASE
notices.text: Walklings nap here between the roots. Whisper, tiptoe, and keep your snack wrappers quiet.

notices.title: SEEN: ONE SLEEPY WALKLING
notices.text: Napping between the roots in Wickerglen. Not lost. Just busy. Please do not wake.

notices.title: LANTERN HOUSE: BEDS READY
notices.text: Garnet keeps the beds in Cobblecrest. A rest is 5 Acorns; with none at all, it's free.

notices.title: BRINEWICK ROAD CLOSED
notices.text: Closed while crates are loaded. The Keepers ask: mind the Pebblits underfoot either way.

notices.title: FOUND: ONE DUSTY GLOVE
notices.text: Found by the quarry path. Smells of stone. A Pebblit has been guarding it. Ask nicely.

notices.title: BRIGHT QUARRY IS OPEN
notices.text: A Glimmerwell Co. site. Clerk Mint is at the desk. It's a partnership! Have a bright day!

notices.title: FALLSTAIR: CLOSED
notices.text: CLOSED FOR SURVEY, says the sign at Hushwater. The Old Weir is still fine for sitting.

notices.title: MAHOPAC: TIME SNAGS
notices.text: Time-snagged woods. If the day feels familiar, it is. Keep your Walkling close.

notices.title: LOST: THE TIME
notices.text: Last seen in Mahopac's woods. Nora, Cal and Bess may have it. Or had it. Hard to say.

notices.title: BRIGHTER BY NATURE
notices.text: Glimmer lanterns: free, friendly, always on. Why sit in the dark? Brighter by nature.

notices.title: IT'S A PARTNERSHIP!
notices.text: Your Walkling is a unit. You are a partner. Together, you're a quarterly target!

notices.title: FEELING TIRED?
notices.text: Tired is just relaxed with bad lighting! Ask any wine vest about Comfort Lamps.

notices.title: CLIMB THE TIERS
notices.text: Guest to Founder's Pick, one quota at a time. Marlowe knows the names at the top.

notices.title: TIER 2? STAY BRIGHT
notices.text: Tier 2 units may feel a soft click of belonging. Totally normal. Have a bright day!

notices.title: YOUR BRINEWICK DEPOT
notices.text: Crates in, crates out, smiles all round. Your harbour depot. It's a partnership!

notices.title: COMFORT SANCTUARY
notices.text: Somewhere restful for every crated unit. Where, exactly? That's the restful part.

notices.title: NOW IN THE CAPITAL
notices.text: Wine vests may be asked to leave. Bright ideas never are. Have a bright day!

notices.title: LANTERN COACH
notices.text: Porters Dunmore and Aldous will see you aboard. Be kind in the streets, and in the queue.

notices.title: CAPITAL LANTERN HOUSE
notices.text: Host Maudie keeps beds ready. Rest is 5 Acorns, or what you have. Fade needs care.

notices.title: KEEPER1 REMINDER
notices.text: Your Keeper1 is active. We can read this. That is the service. Leave a light.

notices.title: WALK SOFT ON ROUTE 3
notices.text: Five Walklings answer the hum here. Walk beside them, not ahead of them.

notices.title: TIDE HALL
notices.text: Master Marisol keeps the Tide Hall and the ferry both. If she's out, sit a while.

notices.title: FOUND: ONE SANDY SCARF
notices.text: Left on a bench by the west pier. Smells of salt. Ask at the Lantern House.

notices.title: SEEN NAPPING
notices.text: One sleepy Walkling, curled on a Canal Marina bench. Not lost, it says. Just resting.

notices.title: LOST: ONE SANDAL
notices.text: Somewhere on the Brinewick road. If a Walkling is chewing it, it may keep it.

notices.title: HEARTHMOOR PLAZA
notices.text: The Keepers' square, west of home. West watch on duty. Read the Plaza sign; it's for you.

notices.title: LANTERN NIGHT
notices.text: On Hearthmoor Plaza. Keep your Walkling close and your lantern low. West watch is about.

notices.title: FOUND: ONE SATCHEL
notices.text: By the Schoolhouse gate. A Walkling is sitting on it like it's a job. Collect gently.

notices.title: KEEPER HOUSE: SEATING
notices.text: A citizen waits in the doorway. A holder is offered a chair. Thank you for knowing which.

notices.title: SCHOOLHOUSE HOURS
notices.text: Lizzy teaches 8-3 on weekdays. Buddy attends, on time. Visitors after 3, please.

notices.title: AMBERHILL FLATS: 5B
notices.text: There's a leak in 5B. Lizzy knows. Mr. Gristle knows. The bucket knows. Mind the drip.

notices.title: ROUTE 1: TALL GRASS
notices.text: Shy Walklings live here. Walk beside, not ahead. The Keepers thank you for quiet feet.

notices.title: SEEN: ONE NAPPING POMLET
notices.text: In the fork of an orchard tree since breakfast. Not lost. Not moving. Please let it be.

notices.title: FERNBROOK LANTERN HOUSE
notices.text: Host Amos has beds and explains healing. 5 Acorns, or what you have. Fade needs care.

notices.title: READ THE MEMO!
notices.text: Associate Tobin follows the memo. So can you! Crates packed with care. Have a bright day!

notices.title: ATTEN, BY DECENT PEOPLE
notices.text: Brewed on the ridge by RegenX, a lab of decent people. Now a partner! Have a bright day!

notices.title: FOUND: ONE WINDBLOWN HAT
notices.text: On the ridge by the old tunnels. The wind wants it back. Claim it before the wind does.

notices.title: FOUND: ONE CLIPBOARD
notices.text: By the Route 2 path near the Glow Census tent. Still looks busy. Please return it.

notices.title: CLIPBOARDS PROVIDED
notices.text: Help the Glow Census on Route 2. Bring your own smile. Brighter by nature!

notices.title: FOUND: ONE KNITTED SCARF
notices.text: Over a root in Wickerglen. A Walkling is napping on it. Collection can wait.

notices.title: LEAVE GLOW WHERE IT GROWS
notices.text: The Wickerglen lamps are off. Walk beside, not ahead. Feed, rest, listen. The Keepers.

notices.title: HEALING, EXPLAINED
notices.text: Garnet will tell you how rest works, then tell you again. The beds are ready either way.

notices.title: FADE: NOT A BED MATTER
notices.text: Lantern Houses do not cure Fade. Care does. Garnet will say so too, kindly.

notices.title: SHOP OPEN
notices.text: Shopkeeper Dottie is in. Mind the Pebblit by the door. It is staff, apparently.

notices.title: SAME STONE, BRIGHTER
notices.text: Bright Quarry, a Glimmerwell Co. site. Brighter by nature. Have a bright day!

notices.title: FOUND: A STONE THAT BLINKS
notices.text: By the Stone Hall door. On closer look, a Pebblit. It does not need finding.

notices.title: SCOUT AT WORK
notices.text: A Keeper scout is mapping Hushwater. Give the scout room, and keep to the path.

notices.title: FOUND: A WATCH, RUNNING
notices.text: Found in Mahopac's woods. It keeps time. The woods do not. Claim it before it snags.

notices.title: OBSERVATORY: LOOK GENTLY
notices.text: The lens remembers. Bring your Walkling: trust comes faster once it sees who you were.

notices.title: TIER 3? BRILLIANT!
notices.text: Three lanyards, one partner, zero hesitation. Next rung: Bright Lead. Have a bright day!

notices.title: SIGNAL REVIEW RECAP
notices.text: Relays reviewed. Partners briefed. A cursor typed LISTEN. So we are! Brightly!

notices.title: SIGN HERE, SHINE ON
notices.text: Crate manifests in Brinewick sign in seconds. Crates travel. You glow. It's a partnership!

notices.title: THE FOUNDER'S LINE
notices.text: Five on the Brinewick road: Quiet, Humming, Answering. Always on. Just like us!

notices.title: WORD OF THE QUARTER
notices.text: Glow sharing: like sharing, but glowier. Questions? Ask your quarterly target!

notices.title: EVENT HALL ENTRY
notices.text: Five games inside. Entry by Warden Ilse's invite. Six regulars. Bring patience.

notices.title: FOUND: ONE MITTEN
notices.text: On a Chapel bench in High Charity. Slightly chewed. The chewer is not sorry.

notices.title: LOST: ONE PENCIL
notices.text: Last seen at the Shipping Ledger Office. With all those pages, it earned a rest.

notices.title: BRINEWICK LANTERN HOUSE
notices.text: Beds for the hurt and tired. 5 Acorns, or what you have. Fade needs care, not beds.

notices.title: SEEN NAPPING: FERRY STEPS
notices.text: One Walkling on the west pier steps. Not lost. The tide's out, so it's sitting a while.

notices.title: STANDING, PLAINLY
notices.text: Care and kindness earn Standing. Trusted holders find a Lantern House bed saved.

notices.title: LOST: HOW IT USED TO BE
notices.text: Ours came back from the facility. Same fur, same name. If you knew it before, call.

notices.title: RELAY HOUSE: THE HUM
notices.text: Do not report the hum. The hum is normal. Reports will be filed.

notices.title: QUARTERLY TARGETS POSTED
notices.text: Befriends, battles won, Census logs, crates packed. Below target means review.

notices.title: RECORDS ROOM: CLOSED
notices.text: Closed for review. Statements filed before the review have been archived.

notices.title: A BRIGHTER BREW
notices.text: Atten, for the partnership. Cheaper soon. Please do not ask where it was first made.

notices.title: CURFEW POSTS STAND
notices.text: By order: posts stay up until the holders here are enrolled. Ask the Lodge.

notices.title: CRATES: DO NOT LIFT LIDS
notices.text: Comfort crates are company property. Walklings inside are resting. Glimmerwell Co.

notices.title: NO SIGNAL PAST THE TRUNK
notices.text: Past the fallen trunk the Keeper wires stop. Tell someone where you are walking.

notices.title: TRIAL LANYARD DAY
notices.text: Try a lanyard, keep the smile! Seals logged free while you wait. Glimmerwell Co.

notices.title: TOWN BOARD: GATE COUNT
notices.text: Officer Cald wants a word about the east sign. Go see him. One tap, one walk.

notices.title: WEST WATCH: A LAP
notices.text: Officer Vale is waiting on the lap: lamps, plaque, chalk. Report back at the watch.

notices.title: LANTERN NIGHT TONIGHT
notices.text: Plaza lamps lit at dusk by Keeper Pryce. Bring a warm drink. Bring a Walkling.

notices.title: FIVE THAT ANSWER
notices.text: Five old Walklings hum along the Brinewick road. Report each one to the Archivist.

notices.title: 5B: MIND THE BUCKET
notices.text: Flat 5B ceiling drips. Bucket in the hall. Please do not kick the bucket.

notices.title: PICKING DAY
notices.text: Every name in the draw. Good luck to all. Your first Walkling may be waiting.

notices.title: TOWPATH: KEEPERS ONLY
notices.text: Canal towpath closed to walkers. The road goes round by the stone bridge.

notices.title: RESURFACED BY PERMIT
notices.text: Roads and Coaches thanks you for keeping to the road. Please mind the walls.

notices.title: LOST: ONE BENCH CUSHION
notices.text: Left at the fork shelter. Last seen under a sleeping Walkling. Keep it, if so.

notices.title: THE LODGE IS IN
notices.text: The Warden would like to hear how it went. Come in person, not on the wire.

notices.title: BY ORDER
notices.text: No gathering after dark at the springs gate. By order of the capital.

notices.title: SPRING GAUGE
notices.text: Another notch down. Please do not tap the glass. It does not help.

notices.title: COMMON GROUND: LEASED
notices.text: Tower stands on common ground by lease. The lease ends at the next sitting.

notices.title: RELOCATED, WITH THANKS
notices.text: A new home down the coast. Post goes to the works office. Have a bright day!

notices.title: HALL 5: KILN COLD
notices.text: No fuel vote, no fire. The Trial Hall waits on the council.

notices.title: BY APPOINTMENT
notices.text: Brightgate HQ welcomes guests to the lobby. All other floors by appointment.

notices.title: GLOW CARE: JOIN TODAY
notices.text: A member clinic for your Walkling. Shut door, open heart. Ask about partnership.

notices.title: HALL 4: OLD WICK
notices.text: The Brightgate Trial Hall is in the old quarter. Follow the flame lanterns.

notices.title: PICKING DAY: SUSPENDED
notices.text: By order: closed to civilians until further notice. Holders are not affected.

notices.title: MUSTER HALL: CHAINED
notices.text: Shut since the Great War. Opens for a holder with seven Seals on the roll.

you.headline: {holder} and {partner}, out walking
body: {holder} and {partner} logged {steps} steps today. Old Meadow sends its regards.
The paper notes no complaints from the grass.

you.headline: {town} has new regulars
body: Folks in {town} say {holder} and {partner} are part of the scenery now. The good part.

you.headline: {partner} looks happy, sources say
body: Keep {partner}'s care at 75 or more and the GLOWING mood shows. Sources say {holder} knows the trick.

you.headline: Market Row has noticed {holder}
body: Word on Market Row: {holder} has Acorns in pocket. Lamplight Provisions is trying to look casual.

you.headline: Seal count for {holder}: {seals}
body: Seals so far for {holder}: {seals}. The level cap climbs with every one.
{partner} has been told. {partner} is very proud.

you.headline: {holder} takes Route 2 at a stroll
body: {holder} and {partner} logged {steps} steps today. The Route 2 gravel has filed no complaints.

you.headline: {partner} keeps the hush in Wickerglen
body: Spotted: {holder} and {partner} tiptoeing between the roots. Nobody woke. The paper approves.

you.headline: {seals} Seals and counting for {holder}
body: Master Hale's Stone Hall saw {holder} and {partner} at work. The Pebblits rolled over in respect.
More Seals, higher level cap. Hale nodded, which for Hale is a standing ovation.

you.headline: {town} has a bed for {holder}
body: {holder} has the Acorns for a Lantern House bed, and {partner} has the yawn. Sounds like a plan.

you.headline: {holder} visits Mahopac. Or did. Or will
body: Time snags in Mahopac's woods. {partner} stuck close to {holder} the whole time, whichever time it was.

you.headline: {holder} rolls into the capital
body: {holder} stepped off the Lantern Coach into High Charity. The lanterns on every roof did not comment.

you.headline: Seen in {town}: {holder}
body: The Keeper wires noticed {holder} in {town} today. Kind in the streets? The Keepers think so.
Your Keeper1 is active. That is the service.

you.headline: {holder} and {partner} sit a while
body: The tide's out at Brinewick, and {holder} and {partner} took the advice. {seals} Seals, zero hurry.

you.headline: {partner} out-walks the Brinewick road
body: {holder} and {partner} logged {steps} steps today. Route 3 is long, and {partner} wants every step.

you.headline: Partner of the quarter: {holder}?
body: {holder} and unit {partner} are trending toward target. Glimmerwell is so proud. Have a bright day!

you.headline: {holder} and {partner} do a Plaza lap
body: Spotted on Hearthmoor Plaza: {holder} and {partner}, nodding at the West watch. The watch nodded back.

you.headline: {partner} approves of the small jobs
body: From the home desk: {holder} keeps doing small jobs with {partner}. Mom says that's how a bond grows.

you.headline: {holder} walks the tall grass
body: {holder} and {partner} logged {steps} steps today. Route 1's shy Walklings watched every one.

you.headline: {holder} wears it kindly
body: Master Fen said 'Wear it kindly.' {town} says {holder} and {partner} are doing just that.
Seal count: {seals}. The level cap has noticed.

you.headline: {holder}'s photo is up at the Pavilion
body: The Bright Pavilion wall has a new face: {holder}, with unit {partner}. Brighter by nature!

you.headline: {holder} walks past the Census tent
body: {holder} and {partner} passed the Glow Census tent. {partner} counted the clipboards instead.

you.headline: Garnet has a bed for {holder}
body: A rest at Garnet's in Cobblecrest is five Acorns, and {holder} has them. {partner} has the yawn ready.
The healing talk comes with it, free, as always.

you.headline: {holder}, apologising to Pebblits
body: {holder} and {partner} logged {steps} steps today. In Cobblecrest, that is a lot of "sorry" to Pebblits.

you.headline: {partner} has seen who {holder} was
body: The lens at Breckenridge showed {holder}'s memories, and {partner} watched too.
A Walkling trusts you faster once it has seen who you were. {partner} is sitting closer.

you.headline: {holder} lifts the lids in Cobblecrest
body: {holder} and {partner} helped three Pebblits out of their crates. Master Hale opened the seam.
Freeing crated Walklings is care and kindness. The Keepers count it.

you.headline: {holder} has an Event Hall invite
body: Ilse's invite has {holder}'s name on it. {partner} has already picked a favourite of the five games.

you.headline: {holder} logs steps; a Tallybat may too
body: {holder} and {partner} logged {steps} steps today. A Tallybat on Route 3 may have counted them.

you.headline: {holder} takes the Tide Hall Seal
body: Marisol's Tide Hall saw {holder} and {partner} win. Then the ferry captain said sit a while. They sat.

you.headline: Tier 3 for {holder}! The neck is crowded
body: {holder} and unit {partner} are three lanyards in. Founder's Pick is up the ladder. Have a bright day!

you.headline: {holder} saw the grey tower too
body: {holder} and {partner} eyed the flat clouds over the grey tower. {partner} looked away first.

you.headline: {holder} worked both shifts in Wickerglen
body: A day with the lamp crew, a dusk with the Keeper Scout. {partner} stayed close both times.

you.headline: Off the wire with {holder}
body: {holder} found the hut past the fallen trunk. No bars, no wires, one kettle. {partner} liked the quiet.

you.headline: {holder} wears two faces this autumn
body: A lanyard on the coat, a Cadet oath underneath. {partner} knows which one is real.

you.headline: Cadet {holder}, on the hill
body: {holder} took the oath at the Lodge. {partner} sat up very straight for it.

you.headline: {holder} walked the west watch
body: Lamps, plaque, chalk, and back to the watch. {partner} inspected the chalk most carefully.

you.headline: {holder} closed the gate count
body: The east sign stands because {holder} went and looked. Small jobs keep a town.

you.headline: {holder} found all five that answer
body: Five old Walklings, five pages in the Archivist's book. {partner} hummed back at the last one.

you.headline: {holder} is home, pin on
body: The lanyard is in a drawer. The pin is on the coat. {partner} sniffed the drawer once and lost interest.

you.headline: {holder} had supper at home
body: Mom, Maze, {partner} and {holder}. Somebody told the truth, or somebody did not. The soup was good.

you.headline: {holder} walked the coach road north
body: Downs, fork, river road, Charter Hill gate. {partner} looked back at Hearthmoor once, then not again.

you.headline: {holder} spotted a heron in the reeds
body: It was a reed until it was not. {partner} saw it first and said nothing, which is very heron of it.

you.headline: {holder} met Governor Merriden
body: Charter Hill, a good chair, a whole town to look at. {partner} waited by the door like a guard.

you.headline: {holder} walked to the lens with Mom
body: The woods were snagged as ever. {partner} stayed close. Neither of you said the next thing.

you.headline: {holder} reached cold Kilnmouth
body: Frost on the pool rims, coats at the bathhouse. {partner} sniffed the springs and sneezed.

you.headline: {holder} holds {seals} Seals now
body: The Kilnmouth kiln burned for {holder} and {partner}. The Master shook hands like he meant it.

you.headline: {holder} earned the Brightgate Seal
body: A Keeper Cadet in the company's own city, and a Seal from Master Ada. {partner} crackled for a minute.

you.headline: {holder} saw the parade
body: Rotors, Officers, the President's car. {partner} hid behind {holder} for the tanks. Fair.

you.headline: {holder} logged {steps} steps today
body: North roads are long. {partner} kept pace with {holder} the whole way.

you.headline: {seals} Seals in the case, and counting
body: {holder} and {partner} hold more Seals than most on the hill. High Charity's roll has them all.

you.headline: Lizzy has a new lesson plan
body: A pupil from the hill came home a Cadet. {holder} is welcome at the back of the class any time.

you.headline: {holder} told it all off the wire
body: Ledger, lamps, the list. Jacob Chi wrote down every word. {partner} slept by the stove.

you.headline: {holder} raced Rook to the Hall door
body: Old Wick, a Junior Bright, one door. {partner} wanted a rematch before the dust settled.
